scenes.tts: Where Koshland argued enzymes must move, David Phillips made one hold still long enough to photograph.

scenes.tts: In 1965 he solved the first atom-by-atom structure of an enzyme — hen egg-white lysozyme, the very structure you can open and rotate from the rail.
scenes.visual: 1965 on a timeline; first atom-by-atom enzyme structure; lysozyme chip; viewer window with rotate arrow.
scenes.narration: In 1965 he solved the first atom-by-atom structure of an enzyme — hen egg-white lysozyme, the very structure you can open and rotate from the rail.

scenes.tts: In a three-day burst of reasoning he saw not just the fold but the mechanism: the enzyme's deep cleft grips the sugar chain of a bacterial cell wall, and the sugar can't fit without bending into a strained "half-chair," wrenched far enough out of true that its bonds are primed to snap.
scenes.visual: Three days; fold vs mechanism; schematic enzyme with cleft, sugar chain tiles, strained tile, link snaps.
scenes.narration: In a three-day burst of reasoning he saw not just the fold but the mechanism: the enzyme's deep cleft grips the sugar chain of a bacterial cell wall, and the sugar can't fit without bending into a strained "half-chair," wrenched far enough out of true that its bonds are primed to snap.

scenes.tts: Catalysis had become a problem in engineering. A wartime radar officer — reading invisible signals bouncing off objects he never saw — he trusted that kind of leap, and pressed a pragmatism on his students: "Don't let the best be the enemy of the good."
scenes.visual: Catalysis to engineering; radar scope with sweep and echoes; leap; students and pragmatism.
scenes.narration: Catalysis had become a problem in engineering. A wartime radar officer — reading invisible signals bouncing off objects he never saw — he trusted that kind of leap, and pressed a pragmatism on his students: "Don't let the best be the enemy of the good."

scenes.tts: The skeletal model he built, 129 amino acids folded at a hundred million times life size, became the picture of an enzyme in every textbook that followed.
scenes.visual: 129 residue dots fold into a blob; scale to a hundred million times; textbooks.
